patch.objective: Removing impediments and managing issues: evaluating impact, prioritizing, applying an intervention strategy, and recognizing when a risk becomes an issue
secondaryObjectives: Leading a project team: setting team-level expectations, empowering the team, solving problems, representing the team's voice, and choosing an appropriate leadership style

sources.cite: PMI, Project Management Professional (PMP) Examination Content Outline, July 2026 Update: People 33%, Process 41%, Business Environment 26%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of a copy of PMI's PDF hosted by a training provider (the course seed cites PMI's own copy). Relevant text: Domain II Task 3 'Help ensure value-based delivery' ('Prioritize work based on value and stakeholder feedback'; 'Assess opportunities to deliver value incrementally'); Task 8 'Plan and manage schedule' ('Baseline a project schedule'; 'Analyze schedule variation'); Domain III Task 3 'Manage and control changes' ('Execute the change control process'); Task 4 'Remove impediments and manage issues' ('Evaluate the impact of impediments'; 'Recognize when a risk becomes an issue'); Task 5 'Plan and manage risk'; Task 8 'Evaluate external business environment changes' ('Assess and prioritize the impact on project scope/backlog based on changes in the external business environment'). The objective wording here is the course seed's.

sources.cite: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland, The Scrum Guide (November 2020)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 directly (the PDF). Daily Scrum: 'The purpose of the Daily Scrum is to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary'; 'a 15-minute event for the Developers of the Scrum Team'.

sources.cite: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland, The Scrum Guide (November 2020)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 directly (the PDF). Scrum Master accountabilities include 'Causing the removal of impediments to the Scrum Team's progress'; the Developers are accountable for 'Creating a plan for the Sprint, the Sprint Backlog' and 'Adapting their plan each day toward the Sprint Goal'.

sources.cite: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland, The Scrum Guide (November 2020)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 directly (the PDF). Definition of Done: 'If a Product Backlog item does not meet the Definition of Done, it cannot be released or even presented at the Sprint Review'; it returns to the Product Backlog for future consideration.

sources.cite: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland, The Scrum Guide (November 2020)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 directly (the PDF). Scrum values: 'Commitment, Focus, Openness, Respect, and Courage'; the three pillars transparency, inspection and adaptation; forecasts such as burn-downs 'do not replace the importance of empiricism'.

sources.cite: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland, The Scrum Guide (November 2020)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 directly (the PDF). Sprint Review: 'a working session and the Scrum Team should avoid limiting it to a presentation'; Retrospective: 'to plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness'.
